# gitattributes: text, binary, eol, and drivers

After this page you can author a `.gitattributes` file that marks text versus binary paths, force `eol=lf` for shell scripts, verify effective attributes with `git check-attr`, and interpret `git ls-files --eol` when a checkout looks wrong on disk.

## Thesis

`.gitignore` answers "do we track this path?". **`.gitattributes`** answers "how should Git treat the bytes?". Without attributes, a Linux-first repo checked out on Windows (or the reverse) quietly rewrites line endings, shell scripts grow `\r`, and binary assets get mangled by text filters. Attributes are the portable contract for a team.

This chapter does **not** re-teach ignore patterns.

Verified with **git 2.47.3**.

## Mental model

```text
  patterns in .gitattributes (last match wins per attribute)
        │
        ├─ text / -text / binary   → normalize EOLs or leave alone
        ├─ eol=lf | eol=crlf       → working-tree line ending
        ├─ diff=<driver>           → how diffs are shown
        ├─ merge=<driver>          → conflict strategy
        └─ filter=<name>           → clean/smudge (advanced)
```

Git stores a normalized form in the object database for `text` paths. The worktree can differ (`eol=*` / `core.autocrlf`). `binary` (macro for `-text -diff`) keeps bytes opaque.

## Lab

<!-- file: attrs-lab.sh -->
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf /tmp/attrs-demo && mkdir /tmp/attrs-demo && cd /tmp/attrs-demo
git init -b main
git config user.name t
git config user.email t@t
printf '*.txt text\n*.bin binary\n*.sh text eol=lf\n' > .gitattributes
printf 'hello\r\n' > f.txt
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho hi\n' > run.sh
printf '\x00\x01\x02' > data.bin
git add .gitattributes f.txt run.sh data.bin
git commit -m 'attrs'
git check-attr -a -- f.txt run.sh data.bin
git ls-files --eol
```

Verified output:

```text
f.txt: text: set
run.sh: text: set
run.sh: eol: lf
data.bin: binary: set
data.bin: diff: unset
data.bin: merge: unset
data.bin: text: unset
i/lf    w/lf    attr/                 	.gitattributes
i/-text w/-text attr/-text            	data.bin
i/lf    w/crlf  attr/text             	f.txt
i/lf    w/lf    attr/text eol=lf      	run.sh
```

## A pragmatic root `.gitattributes`

```gitattributes
* text=auto
*.sh text eol=lf
*.bash text eol=lf
*.bat text eol=crlf
*.cmd text eol=crlf
*.png binary
*.jpg binary
*.pdf binary
*.wasm binary
```

`text=auto` lets Git guess for unmatched paths. Be explicit for shells and binaries you care about.

## Drivers (short)

Named `diff` and `merge` drivers are configured under `diff.<name>.*` / `merge.<name>.*` and referenced from attributes (`*.c diff=cpp`). Custom drivers are powerful and easy to get wrong — introduce them only when the default three-way merge is not enough (generated lockfiles, union merges).

## Renormalizing after a policy change

Changing attributes does not rewrite historical blobs by itself. When you intentionally want the index to match the new rules:

```bash
git add --renormalize .
git status
git commit -m 'chore: renormalize line endings'
```

Coordinate with the team: every checkout will see a large diff once.

## Pitfalls

1. Marking binaries as `text` corrupts content when EOLs flip.
2. Pattern order — more specific rules should come after broad ones when you need overrides.
3. Mixing `core.autocrlf=true` with detailed attributes without documenting which wins in your environment.
4. Checking in editor-specific end-of-line settings instead of attributes.

## Summary

- Use `.gitattributes` for text/binary/eol policy; verify with `check-attr` and `ls-files --eol`.
- Force `eol=lf` on shell scripts; mark media `binary`.
- Renormalize deliberately and as a team when policy changes.


## Worked scenarios

### Scenario A — stop CRLF noise on shell scripts
A contributor on Windows commits `deploy.sh` with CRLF. Linux CI fails with `/bin/bash^M`. Fix:

```gitattributes
*.sh text eol=lf
```

Then renormalize once as a team.

### Scenario B — keep PNGs untouched
```gitattributes
*.png binary
*.jpg binary
*.webp binary
```

Without this, `text=auto` might still treat some binaries oddly on exotic setups; being explicit is cheap.

### Scenario C — custom diff for lockfiles
```gitattributes
package-lock.json merge=ours
```

paired with a merge driver that always keeps the current branch's lockfile during release branches — document heavily before using.

## Attributes versus `core.autocrlf`

| Setting | Scope | Portability |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| `core.autocrlf` | Local machine config | Easy to diverge across clones |
| `.gitattributes` | Committed with the repo | Same rules for everyone |

Prefer attributes for team policy; leave autocrlf off (`input` or `false`) when attributes own EOL.

## Common mistakes (extended)

- Committing `.gitattributes` changes without renormalizing — half the tree still has old index modes.
- Using `eol=crlf` on Linux-only scripts "just in case".
- Expecting attributes to affect ignored (untracked) files — they apply to tracked paths.
